# Turn log no longer displays

**Regression:** the in-game **Activity Log** panel ("turn log") no longer displays its
entries.

## Problem statement

Players can no longer see the Activity Log panel content, so they lose the running
record of each turn's income, incidents and actions. This is a regression on `dev`
(v0.1.19) and is filed as `critical`.

## Users

- **Main Street players (single-player)** — need the per-turn record to understand
  what happened each turn.
- **Tutorial players** — rely on the log feedback while learning the loop.
- **Competitive players** — need the per-seat action transcript.

Example user stories:

- As a single-player, I want the Activity Log to show each turn's entries as they
  happen, so that I can follow the state of the game.
- As a tutorial player, I want the log to remain visible while the tutorial runs, so
  that I can connect tutorial actions to their outcomes.
- As a competitive player, I want the log to show both seats' actions, so that I can
  follow an AI-vs-AI or mixed match.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Activity Log panel renders its entries when the scene loads and updates after each turn completes, in **single-player, tutorial and competitive** modes.
- A new automated test reproduces the blank-log failure on the pre-fix revision and passes after the fix (browser test preferred; supplement with unit coverage where the timing contract is involved). The introducing commit is identified (e.g. via `git bisect` or commit-diff inspection) and the fix restores the pre-regression behaviour without changing documented log content or order.
- The two currently-failing tests in `tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts` (deferral window) pass; their assertion helper must read Phaser `Text.text` correctly (it currently reads `c.text?.text`, which is always `undefined`).
- The deferred-rendering contract is preserved: entries accumulated during end-of-turn closing still appear **after** the upcoming/phase UI, never before it (MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2).
- Log scrolling/auto-scroll behaviour is unchanged (auto-scroll to newest, no yank when the player has scrolled up).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (unit plus the browser project, run explicitly).

## Constraints

- Must not break the deferred log-render ordering contract (MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2).
- Keep positioning SLL-driven (`src/layouts/main-street.layout.json`); no hard-coded
  pixel coordinates.
- The Phaser/browser context is shared and sensitive: browser tests run serially.
- CI (`npm test`) runs **only** the `unit` Vitest project; `*.browser.test.ts` files
  are excluded. Any browser-level regression coverage must be run explicitly via
  `npx vitest run --project browser` and should be noted as such.

## Existing state

- The Activity Log panel is created once in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` (title text `Activity Log`).
- Content is rendered by `refreshLog` in `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts`, which
  is called from `refreshAll`.
- Deferred rendering is gated by `logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete`, set/cleared in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`
  (`finishTurnPresentation` / `finalizeTurn` → `flushDeferredLog`).
- Log panel state is reset on scene restart in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`.
- On `dev` HEAD (`b3a9941`):
  - `tests/main-street/activity-log.test.ts` (42 tests) and
    `tests/main-street/activity-log-deferred-rendering.test.ts` (6 tests) **pass**.
  - `npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts`
    → **2 failed | 15 passed** (re-confirmed by the intake session). The failing cases
    are the deferral-window tests ("suppresses new entry rendering while
    `logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete` is set" and "keeps accumulated entries in order
    when rendered after the deferral window"); the failures are caused by the
    assertion helper reading `c.text?.text` (always `undefined` for a Phaser `Text`,
    whose rendered string is the `.text` property itself), which means this browser
    coverage never actually verified the rendered text.
  - Note: `npm test` runs only the `unit` project, so these browser failures do not
    appear in the default suite.

## Desired change

Restore the Activity Log display and make the regression detectable:

1. Identify and fix the root cause of the blank/missing log (prime suspects: the
   deferred-rendering gate never being lifted on some path, or a recent boot/turn-flow
   change on `dev`).
2. Correct the deferral-window browser test helper so it reads the rendered text
   correctly, and add explicit coverage that the log is non-empty on scene load and
   after a turn in each mode.
3. Keep deferral ordering and scroll behaviour intact.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — `refreshLog` deferral gate, entry rendering
  and scroll bounds; likely fix site.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — sets/clears
  `logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete`; verify every path flushes.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — log state fields (`logPrevEntryCount`,
  `logAutoScroll`, `logScrollOffset`, …) and `refreshLog` wrapper.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — Activity Log panel creation.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — log state reset on restart.
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts` — fix helper; add
  blank-log regression test.
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-deferred-rendering.test.ts` — deferral timing
  coverage (unit).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (confirmed by producer):** "turn log" means the in-game Activity Log
  panel — the only in-game log that lists per-turn entries. The panel and its title
  bar are visible, but the content area is empty and never fills.
- **Risk:** the symptom may only reproduce in the packaged Electron build or a
  specific mode; confirm repro before assuming the fix site.
- **Risk:** fixing the stale browser assertions may reveal the deferral gate really is
  left set on a path not covered by the unit suite.
- **Risk (scope creep):** a log UI redesign is out of scope; record extra ideas as
  linked work items.
- **Risk:** CI does not run browser tests, so a browser-only regression can recur;
  note explicit browser-run expectation in the fix.

## Related work

### Directly related (context / possible cause)

- **MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2** – Activity Log should not show log line until the results
  have been shown in the UI (completed). Introduced the `logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete`
  gate and the deferral-window browser tests.
- **MS-0MT3JK16W006A66P** – fire banking hint during the tutorial (gate flip + dead-end
  fix) (most recent functional commit on `dev`; touched the turn flow).
- **MS-0MV0OK0XU0062E0H** – Main Street pack listing UI & boot wiring (changed renderer
  and boot).
- **MS-0MV031AYI007UZ7X** – boot/New Game selector ordering
  (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`, `MainStreetScene.ts`).
- **MS-0MV0319OC002H15F** – Reorder tutorial-offer boot flow.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUNO0M2I004TK04** – Wire Main Street challenges to Steam achievements (open)
- **MS-0MUWE6NCA008LDXM** – Two-column Game Over overlay (completed)
- **MS-0MUZ9O1I00088JF2** – Pedestrians seek the nearest occupied cell (including mid-turn fills) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, action, actions, actually, add (+248 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, action, actions, actually, add (+211 more)
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: action, actions, activity, actually, add (+173 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Which surface is "the turn log"? Options: (A) whole panel missing; (B)
  panel/title show but content empty/never updates; (C) turn-specific rows
  missing; (D) other.
  — Answer (operator): **B** — the panel and title show, but the content area is
  empty and never updates. Source: interactive reply (intake session
  `herdr-1791559913-2763730-24821`).
- Q: Where and in which mode is it broken? Options: (A) single-player only; (B)
  competitive only; (C) all modes; (D) not sure.
  — Answer (operator): **C** — all modes. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: What is the visible trigger and when did it last work? Options: (A) broken
  from the first turn / on a fresh game; (B) stops after the first End Turn; (C)
  only after loading a save; (D) only under tutorial / reduced-motion; (E) not
  sure.
  — Answer (operator): **A** — broken from the very first turn / on a fresh
  game; described as a "very recent break". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: Does the blank log reproduce in the automated suite? — Research (intake
  session, `dev` HEAD `b3a9941`): `npm test` (unit project) **passes**; the
  explicit browser run
  `npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts`
  → **2 failed | 15 passed**, but both failures stem from the stale assertion
  helper (`c.text?.text`), so the suite neither proves nor disproves the
  producer-reported blank log. Source: local run; see "Existing state".

> **Prior-session note:** an earlier intake run (`herdr-1791560667-2819121-4932`)
> drafted this brief but left the three questions above as OPEN QUESTIONs and set
> `needsProducerReview=true`. The producer has now answered them; this appendix
> supersedes those OPEN QUESTIONs.

### Plan session (herdr-1791566842-3344279-31129)

- Q: Are new clarifying questions needed to decompose this work item?
  — Answer (plan, agent): **No.** The intake Appendix answers (surface = panel/
  title visible with empty content; scope = all modes; trigger = broken from the
  first turn on a fresh game) already scope the plan, so no new producer questions
  were raised. Source: intake Appendix above; agent reasoning.
- Q: Is a producer plan-approval gate required?
  — Answer (plan, agent): **No.** The effort/risk pre-check returned
  `decision: "plan"` (effort Small, risk High) and the approval gate returned
  `request_approval: false` — approval is only requested for Extra Large effort
  **and** High/Severe risk. Source: `plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed` and
  `plan-approval-gate`.
- Q: Why is the regression test created before the fix?
  — Answer (plan, agent): the AC requires an automated test that reproduces the
  blank-log failure on the pre-fix revision and the introducing commit to be
  identified; the fix depends on that diagnosis. Source: parent AC2/AC3.

> **Plan-session decision (formatting):** the parent Acceptance Criteria list was
> reformatted from a numbered multi-line list to single-line markdown bullets so
> the shared AC-coverage and audit tooling (which parses `- ` bullets) can verify
> coverage. Wording and intent are unchanged.
>
> **Known gap (OPEN QUESTION for the implementing agent):** an automated browser
> repro of the producer-reported blank log has not yet been demonstrated — the
> browser harness logs `Phaser.GameObjects.Components.Mask.setMask: This method
> is not supported in WebGL`, and the existing browser log test passes. The
> test-first child work item must pin the introducing commit before the fix
> child is started. Directed to: the implementing agent; why it matters: the
> fix must target the true root cause, not the stale assertion helper alone.

# Remote hosting of card packs (remote bundle source)

**Related:** `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` (Make card packs available in the browser
distribution — introduces the pack-source registry this builds on)
**Related:** `MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` (Make card-pack assets self-contained)

## Summary

Card packs are currently discovered from a single source: a content directory
(the Electron launcher) or, once `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` lands, a bundled
build-time registry. This item adds a **remote pack source** so a pack catalogue
can be hosted at a URL and fetched at runtime — enabling packs to be published
or updated without rebuilding or re-releasing the game.

This is the future-work half of the source-registry design: the registry seam
(`PackSource[]`) is introduced by `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`, and this item
implements the remote provider on top of it.

## Goal (user story)

> As a distribution operator, I want to host a card pack (and its catalogue) at
> a URL, so I can publish or update packs for an installed game without
> rebuilding the launcher or the web build.

> As a player, I want a remote pack to appear in the Card Packs panel and
> behave exactly like a bundled or content-directory pack (lock → purchase →
> enable → deal), while the game still boots and plays offline on its bundled
> packs if the remote host is unreachable.

## Scope

1. **Remote source provider.** Implement a `PackSource` that fetches a pack
   manifest from a configured URL (via the loader's existing `fetchManifest` /
   `fetchCsv` transports) and contributes its packs to the merged pool.
2. **Configuration.** Define how remote source URLs are declared — a build-time
   config constant, a launcher-provided setting, or a well-known manifest URL —
   and how multiple remote sources compose with bundled/static ones.
3. **Merge and precedence.** Define ordering and conflict handling when the same
   pack id appears in more than one source (bundled wins? first wins? reject
   duplicates?). The core merge contract already rejects duplicate card ids
   whole; pack-id precedence must be decided explicitly.
4. **Gating.** Remote packs remain content-unlock gated; the unlock target key
   and the scoped simulated-purchase flow apply unchanged. Decide whether remote
   packs may be ungated.
5. **Degradation.** A remote host that is slow, unreachable or serving a
   malformed manifest must degrade to the bundled/static packs with a warning —
   never block boot, never blank the listing. Define a timeout.
6. **Trust and integrity.** Address the supply-chain surface: remote packs
   inject card rows into the pool, and the merge contract validates the header
   and duplicate ids but not malicious content. Define an integrity mechanism
   (signing, checksum pinning, allow-listed host/ids) and what the game does
   when verification fails.
7. **Caching / offline.** Decide whether remote packs are cached (for example in
   `localStorage` / Cache Storage) so a previously fetched pack remains usable
   offline, and how cache invalidation/versioning works.
8. **Docs and tests.** Cover remote discovery, degradation, gating and
   integrity with tests, and document the remote-hosting contract.

## Acceptance criteria (to be confirmed at intake)

1. A pack catalogue hosted at a configured URL is discovered at runtime and its
   packs appear in the Card Packs panel.
2. Remote packs behave identically to bundled packs across lock → purchase →
   enable → deal, and save/load.
3. With the remote host unreachable/slow, the game boots on bundled packs and
   warns; the listing is never empty when a bundled pack exists.
4. A malformed remote manifest or a pack with a bad header/duplicate id is
   rejected whole with a warning, without affecting other sources.
5. Pack-id precedence across sources is deterministic and documented.
6. The integrity mechanism rejects a tampered/unverified remote pack and
   documents the failure mode.
7. Remote pack art resolves and renders (coordinated with
   `MS-0MV26K321003MWO0`).
8. Documentation covers configuration, the hosting contract, integrity and
   degradation.
9. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Out of scope

- A pack storefront, purchase/checkout, or pack-authoring UI.
- A pack CDN/build-publish pipeline (a natural follow-up).
- Real money/Steam storefront transactions.
- Changing the bundled or content-directory sources.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — supply chain.** Remote content is untrusted; without integrity
  checks a hostile pack could inject arbitrary card data. Mitigation: signing /
  checksum pinning / host allow-list, with a safe refusal mode.
- **Risk — boot latency.** A remote fetch on the boot path could stall the game.
  Mitigation: bounded timeout, non-blocking discovery, bundled-first.
- **Risk — offline regression.** A user who once fetched a remote pack may lose
  it offline. Mitigation: explicit caching decision.
- **Assumption — registry seam exists.** `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` provides the
  `PackSource` abstraction; this item adds a provider rather than re-architecting.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — remote source registration and merge ordering.
- `core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts` — URL contentDir / transport use.
- `core/src/core-engine/CardPackManifest.ts` — manifest parse (shared).
- `vite.config.ts` / config — remote source URL declaration.
- `tests/main-street/` — remote discovery, degradation, integrity tests.
- `README.md`, `packs/README.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md` — remote-hosting contract.

**discovered-from:MS-0MV53CFUS004DFX1**

**Symptom.** A concurrent push advanced `origin/dev` while `implement.py finish` was committing. The push failed non-fast-forward and the recovery branch in `phase_finish` crashed with `Unhandled exception: name 'cwd' is not defined` (the `git rebase origin/dev` call uses `cwd=cwd`, but `phase_finish` has no `cwd` local). The work item was reset to `open` and the commit was left unpushed (the worktree was already removed), requiring manual rebase/push recovery.

**Location.** `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py`, the `PushNonFastForwardError` handler inside `phase_finish`.

**Expected.** The recovery path rebases onto `origin/dev`, retries the push, and preserves state on failure — without an unhandled exception.

**Suggested fix.** Use the discovered `worktree_path` for the rebase `cwd` (or defer the rebase to a temp worktree); add a regression test.
data.title: implement.py non-fast-forward push recovery references undefined cwd

discovered-from:MS-0MV53CH78004I2BF

Discovered during MS-0MV53CH78004I2BF (Documentation for browser pack distribution).

When implement.py finish pushes to dev and the push is rejected as non-fast-forward (a concurrent agent advanced dev), the retry/rebase path raises an unhandled NameError: name 'cwd' is not defined instead of rebasing and retrying. The commit stays local on the feature branch and the work item is safety-reset to open, forcing manual recovery (git rebase origin/dev && git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev).

Evidence (aborting run stderr):
INFO: Push failed (non-fast-forward); attempting rebase and retry ...
ERROR: Unhandled exception: name 'cwd' is not defined
INFO: Safety reset: MS-0MV53CH78004I2BF status in-progress -> open

Location: the PushNonFastForwardError handling branch in skill/implement/scripts/implement.py (phase_finish retry path) references 'cwd' where the local variable is worktree_path/repo_root. Correct the reference and add a regression test.
data.title: implement.py non-fast-forward push retry crashes with NameError: cwd is not defined
